label: Past Simple vs Present Perfect
outcome: Lo studente sceglie tra Past Simple e Present Perfect partendo dal rapporto tra evento passato e presente: tempo passato finito, esperienza fino ad ora, risultato attuale e periodo ancora aperto.
must_master: finished past time versus connection to now
specific finished past time markers require Past Simple at this level
life experience without a stated finished time uses Present Perfect
a current result can motivate Present Perfect when no finished past time is stated
unfinished current time versus finished past time period
switch from Present Perfect experience/result to Past Simple when asking or giving a specific finished-time detail
build the chosen tense correctly after making the meaning decision

scope_boundary.time_adverbs: Do not turn this topic into the dedicated ever/never, just/already/yet, for/since lesson. Use only transparent contrastive time contexts needed to decide the tense.
scope_boundary.advanced_nuance: Teach the standard school-level contrast. Do not introduce dialectal or discourse-level exceptions where either tense may be acceptable.
scope_boundary.present_perfect_continuous: Do not introduce Present Perfect Continuous.
scope_boundary.narrative_tenses: Do not introduce Past Continuous or Past Perfect contrast here.

decision_model: Is a specific finished past time stated or clearly completed? → Past Simple.
Is this life experience up to now with no finished time stated? → Present Perfect.
Is a past event important because of its result now, with no finished past time stated? → Present Perfect.
Is the time period still open? → Present Perfect can be appropriate; if the period is finished, use Past Simple.
After choosing the tense, check its form separately.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using Present Perfect with a specific finished past time
using Past Simple for life experience when no finished time is given
keeping Present Perfect when a follow-up asks when the event happened
choosing from one signal word without checking whether the time period is finished
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: treating this week as an automatic Present Perfect trigger even after the week has been framed as finished

italian_learner_risks.risk: choosing the correct tense meaning but building the wrong form

context_bank: life experience followed by a specific detail question
a lost item with a present consequence followed by where/when it happened
a completed school trip versus experiences from school trips in general
a current problem caused by a recent event
messages and short dialogues where the speaker moves from general experience to a specific past event
school-style mixed tense completion with unambiguous time context

requirements: teach the meaning decision before signal words
include experience followed by a specific Past Simple detail
include unfinished versus finished time period
five scaffolded graded checks after teaching
at least one item must require tense choice and correct form together
mix experience, result, finished-time and unfinished-time contexts
include one dialogue that switches from Present Perfect to Past Simple for a specific detail
include one Italian-to-English translation using both tenses
avoid dedicated ever/never, already/yet, for/since drilling
no coaching or rule labels that reveal the answer
cover a Present Perfect-to-Past Simple detail switch
test correct tense form as well as tense choice
include one controlled production or translation item

quality_rejections: a worksheet where tense choice is reducible to circling yesterday versus ever
ambiguous contexts where both tenses are defensible in standard English
Present Perfect with a specific finished past time in an answer key
Past Simple used for a general life-experience statement with no finished time unless context clearly frames a completed life period
systematic teaching of the later time-expression syllabus
more than two consecutive isolated tense-choice sentences
difficulty created by vocabulary rather than tense meaning
